about: Real defects GitHub Copilot found in this repo's own PRs, each confirmed and fixed afterwards. A case replays the commit Copilot reviewed as a factory job: base is the PR's merge base, head the reviewed commit. Line ranges are in head. A finding that cites a defect's lines finds it only if it also uses one of its terms.

defects.description: `board.mjs runner` reports only the scheduler lock, so while `run --job` or `rework` holds a job lock the session thinks no runner is live and can drive the same job a second time.
Backlog commands still run in the session while a runner is live, and the session appends to backlog.md without the backlog lock, so claimBacklogItem's read-rewrite can drop the appended task.

Stale-lock recovery renames the lock aside after reading its pid; another process can replace the lock in between, and a third can take the vacant path before the mismatch is noticed, so two live holders enter the critical section.
withLockAsync checks the abort signal only while waiting, so an abort during the sleep followed by a successful acquire still runs fn (it can merge after Ctrl+C).
Agents run detached and survive a crashed runner, but the job lock records only the runner's pid, so a restarted runner reclaims the job and starts a second agent in the same worktree.
ship() deletes the job branch before recording stage merged; a crash in between leaves an approval-stage job whose re-ship fails on the missing branch and lands in needs-human.
Staging and committing the job record go through gitTry, which swallows failures, and the job is still marked merged, so a rejected commit leaves the record uncommitted and never retried.
The backlog item is ticked before the job is created on the board; a crash in between loses the task for good, since restart resumes only board jobs and claims only unticked items.
`run --job` or `run --job=` leaves opts.job empty, so main() takes the no-job branch and runs (and merges) the whole queue instead of rejecting the command.

approve and rework check the needs-human stage and act without the job lock, so two approvals (or approve and rework) race; the second fails on the deleted branch and flips a merged job back to needs-human.
On resume the next action comes from the files, but verdicts written before a crash are never put back on the board, so a job can finish with reviewers still pending there.

A check waiting for a limiter slot is handed the slot when the running check is killed on abort, and spawns with an already-aborted signal; the abort listener added afterwards never fires, so it runs unstoppable.
drive()'s finally removes the activity file with an rmSync that can throw, which skips unlock(lock) and keeps the job locked while the runner carries on.

A crashed runner's activity file stops changing, so pollActivity's equality check never triggers a render; with a drawer open the 30s render timer is off too, and the dead step shows as running forever.

cases.title: UI probe, checkable reviews and static gates
cases.head: 5264e53fba583e991b5e2659776baa369d17c729

defects.description: Failed-request URLs (and console and page-error text) are recorded whole in probe.json and probe.md, which are committed with the job, so tokens and signed-URL credentials leak.
A focus trap on the first Tab stop is reported as a complete walk: the repeated stop equals stops[0], so the completion check fires before the trap check.
The dependency guard diffs the merge base against HEAD, missing uncommitted or untracked manifest and lockfile changes when the builder runs the probe, so the base borrows the wrong node_modules.
When neither the head nor the base app starts, the probe returns an error report with no finding, so reviews proceed without answering the startup failure.

addedLines takes the path from the +++ line as is, so a path with a space keeps git's trailing tab and a quoted path (non-ASCII) is dropped; new lint problems there count as older and a lines-scoped gate passes.
numberDiff prints a file only from its ---/+++ headers, so mode changes, new-file modes and pure renames, which have none, vanish from the diff every reviewer reads.
runAxe keeps only the first five nodes per rule before the base comparison, so a sixth violation the change adds matches the base's five and is never reported.
Screenshot names are slugs of path, state, width and theme, so distinct visits such as /a-b and /a/b overwrite one file and check-review accepts it for both.
planVisits cuts visits at ui.maxVisits, and a screen/state that loses every visit isn't added to unreached, so check-review never asks about it.
A symlink left by an earlier run is accepted without the ignore check new links get, so after ignore rules change a now-committable link passes preparation.
A lines-scoped gate that exits non-zero passes whenever no parsed problem is on a changed line, even if its output also has a fatal config or runtime error.
